assumptions: The initial service forwards orders and does not hold inventory.
At least two distributors permit lawful use of sufficiently current catalog and availability data.
The public EU platform does not provide complete transaction-grade parts availability and SLA prediction.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Signed distributor data terms, a 20-shop pilot demonstrating frequent searches and paid conversion, measurable reductions in quote and completion time, positive margin after returns and support, and clarity on overlap with the public EU platform.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Reliable compatibility, availability, price, and delivery information at quote time addresses a concrete bottleneck between repair demand and completion.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Stalled jobs consume repairer time and revenue, but evidence of Polish shops paying subscriptions or commissions for sourcing intelligence is absent.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Subscriptions plus commissions diversify revenue and avoid inventory initially, but catalog normalization, supplier commissions, low order values, returns, disputes, support, and thin transaction margins may erode economics.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One appliance category, two distributors, and 20 shops is a sensible beachhead, although repair frequency and achievable revenue per shop remain unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A cross-brand graph could lead a fragmented niche, but manufacturers and major distributors control the essential data and fulfillment and can improve their own tools.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning one category enables additional appliances, electronics, geographies, repair quoting, warranty routing, logistics, and refurbished-part supply.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Observed compatibility and delivery performance can compound, but access is nonexclusive and replaceable, with no current catalog rights or transaction density.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A dependable cross-brand answer at quote time could substantially improve turnaround and conversion versus manual catalog searches, provided the data is complete and current.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Right-to-repair obligations taking effect and the planned EU repair platform create a strong market-shaping moment, though the public platform may also absorb discovery value.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Distributor channels and repair associations offer leverage, but the founder has no supplier, shop, or association access and distributors may prefer direct ownership.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A forwarding pilot is capital-feasible and technically aligned, but data licensing, normalization, counterfeit risk, returns, fulfillment disputes, and ongoing catalog operations are substantial.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure transaction-grade catalog and inventory feeds from a distributor consortium with preferred fulfillment economics, making the exchange their cross-brand shop-facing channel rather than an unprivileged overlay.
main_structural_strength: A cross-brand compatibility and observed-delivery graph can improve with transactions and support multiple adjacent repair workflows.
primary_score_limiter: The business depends on supplier-controlled data and fulfillment without holding access rights, while transaction frequency and margin per shop remain unvalidated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The planned public European repair platform may solve discovery, and parts-data rights holders may refuse access.
